name: AWS Neuron: dtype and configuration tradeoffs for inference
arithmetic_intensity: Inferentia2 supports FP32, TF32, BF16, FP16, UINT8, and cFP8 (configurable FP8). Trainium2 adds FP8 at 1300 TFLOPS per chip. The auto-cast path takes FP32/FP16 models and casts down to BF16/FP8/cFP8 at compile time. Stochastic rounding is available to protect accuracy. The dtype choice directly affects throughput: FP8 is 2x FP16 on paper, but real speedup depends on the model and whether the compiler can effectively use the lower precision.
scales_with: precision (FP32 -> BF16 -> FP8, each step changes throughput)

notes: The dtype tradeoff is the primary performance knob for AWS Neuron. The auto-cast path is designed for productivity: 'Autocasting reduces time to market by removing the need for lower-precision retraining.' For maximum performance, manual FP8 configuration with stochastic rounding gives the best throughput but requires accuracy validation. The Neuron Explorer tool provides profiling and AI-powered recommendations for dtype and sharding configuration.
